content: 1. To edit an existing page, first type the topic you are interested in into the search box located in the left panel of the page. 2. Clicking the search button will look for the keyword you entered across all pages, not just in the titles. 3. Once you find the page you want to edit, click the edit button at the top of the page. Alternatively, you can click the edit button in the upper right corner of a specific section to edit only that section. 4. If a topic has multiple names or abbreviations, you may need to redirect them all to a single page. For example, the page ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction can be accessed through redirects from STEMI, MI, Acute MI, Myocardial Infarction, and AMI. 5. To redirect a page (e.g., Page A) to another page (e.g., Page B, the target page), you need to enter a redirecting command at the top of the redirecting page. For instance, to redirect the MI page to the ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction page, edit the MI page and enter the appropriate redirect command. 6. To redirect a page to a specific section within another page, you must enter a redirecting command that specifies the target section. For example, to redirect the Holosystolic Murmur page to the Holosystolic (Pansystolic) Murmurs section in the Heart Murmur page, edit the Holosystolic Murmur page and enter the appropriate command. 7. If you misspell the name of a page, such as ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction, regular users cannot move the page along with its history. Instead, you must create a new page with the correct spelling, manually copy the content from the old page, and then edit the old page to replace its source code with a redirect command. 8. Avoid creating redirects that point to another redirect. These are undesirable because they do not work properly, slow down navigation, create a poor user experience, and make the site's structure confusing. 9. To change the color of text, you can use specific commands. For example, typing a command for red text will yield red-colored text. You can also use hexadecimal color codes to create text in any desired color. 10. To display computer code for teaching purposes, enclose the content with specific tags before and after the code. 11. To change the font size, use sizes ranging from 1 to 7. The default size is 3 unless otherwise specified. For example, typing a command for size 4 will create a larger font, while other commands can increase or decrease the font size relative to the default. 12. To change the typeface of a font, you can use specific commands. For instance, typing a command for the Courier font will display text in that typeface. 13. To insert an image, follow the instructions provided on the relevant help page. 14. To insert references, refer to the appropriate section on how to add references. 15. To add a page to a category, include a line of code specifying the category. For example, adding a line for the Cardiology category will classify the page accordingly. It is customary to place these lines near the bottom of the page. Once saved, the page will be added to the specified category. 16. To insert a table of contents, add the appropriate text within the page. To remove a table of contents, use a specific command to suppress it. 17. For long pages with multiple sections, you can create a Return to top link to allow readers to navigate back to the top without scrolling. This requires knowing the page name and the top section name. 18. To upload a file for others to download, click Upload file in the toolbox menu and follow the instructions. 19. To create a link to the uploaded file, type the appropriate command referencing the file. 20. To edit the left sidebar, type mediawiki:sidebar in the search box. Note that this function may be restricted to administrators. 21. To create a direct link to a picture, use the appropriate syntax. 22. To add large quotes around a section of text, use the cquote template. 23. To upload slides or slide sets for downloading, first upload the slides to the server using the Upload file button. Then, follow the instructions to generate a link to the uploaded slides. 24. To add a Twitter feed, follow the instructions provided in the relevant section. 25. For more advanced editing tools, consider using JavaScript-based tools or other sophisticated options.
